name: Tony Jashanmal
current_role: Group President, Jashanmal Group (Dubai); member of the Executive Board
profile: Kuwait-born (1947) scion of the Jashanmal family, whose Gulf trading/retail group dates back more than a century and distributes and retails books, fashion, accessories, home and electronics brands across the GCC. He joined in 1971 and led diversification into print media, accessories and fashion, post-Gulf War rebuilding in Kuwait and JV entry into India; he still sits on the Executive Board.
interesting_fact: He holds a Diplom-Volkswirt (Master's in Economics) from Hamburg University in Germany, after schooling in India and high school in Villars, Switzerland.
deep_cut_fact: He personally played a key role in rebuilding the group's Kuwait operations after the 1990-91 Gulf War, and has long championed e-commerce at the century-old retailer ('We have embraced technology wholeheartedly at Jashanmal').
notes: Hurun listing ended 2019. Day-to-day leadership: Group CEO is Shuja Jashanmal per the leadership page; Tony is Group President. Contact form is the retail customer form; no published press email found.

name: Xu Rongmao
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Shimao Group Holdings (HKEX: 813); son Jason Hui Sai Tan has been chairman and president since 2024
profile: Xu Rongmao (Hui Wing Mau), born 1950 in Shishi, Fujian, built Shimao into one of China's big property developers, known for Shanghai riverside towers and hotels. He remains Shimao's controlling shareholder via Gemfair and Shiying Finance, but handed the chairmanship to his son in 2024 as the company worked through a debt restructuring.
interesting_fact: He earned a business master's degree by distance learning from the University of Adelaide.
deep_cut_fact: His first big project in his Fujian hometown started out registered as a knitting factory because private hotel investment was banned. When it was finished, the policy had changed, and he ended up owning what Wikipedia calls China's first private three-star hotel.
notes: He keeps a very low profile. Shimao is in a debt restructuring, and per Mingtiandi (July 2026) the CSRC proposed disclosure fines on him and his son. Any outreach would go through Shimao IR/media relations. The deep-cut fact rests only on Wikipedia, whose early-life details are partly tagged 'citation needed'.

name: Vadim Novinsky
current_role: Founder/beneficiary of Smart Holding Group (Ukraine; ownership contested after 2022 trust transfer); former Ukrainian MP; protodeacon of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church
profile: Novinsky was born in Russia in 1963, rose through Lukoil's North-West division in the 1990s, then bought Ukrainian metallurgy assets and co-founded Smart Holding in 2006, which holds a minority stake in Metinvest. He became a Ukrainian citizen in 2012 and was an MP from 2013 to 2022. He left Ukraine in 2023 and was reportedly granted Serbian citizenship in 2026.
interesting_fact: An active patron of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church, he was reportedly ordained a deacon by Metropolitan Onufriy in 2020 and serves as a protodeacon.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in aviation, not metals: he graduated in 1985 from the Leningrad Academy of Civil Aviation in engineering management systems.
notes: HIGH RISK, not recommended for outreach. He is under Ukrainian NSDC sanctions (Dec 2022/Jan 2023) and was charged in absentia with high treason in January 2025; he calls the charges politically motivated. He lives outside Ukraine (reportedly Serbian citizenship, 2026). Control of Smart Holding is disputed after the Justice Ministry cancelled the trust transfer. No published contact found.

name: Christina Ong
current_role: Founder-owner, COMO Group (COMO Hotels and Resorts, COMO Shambhala, Club 21), Singapore
profile: Christina Ong, born in 1948 and the daughter of oil trader Peter Fu Yun Siak, opened luxury boutique Club 21 in Singapore in 1972 and built it into an international fashion retail group. She bought her first hotel, The Halkin in London, in 1991, created the COMO hotel and COMO Shambhala wellness brands, and took control of Mulberry in 2002. In 2026 COMO opened new properties on the French Riviera and in Bordeaux.
interesting_fact: She founded Club 21 at age 24 as a small boutique in Singapore's Tanglin Shopping Centre. The group grew to about 400 luxury fashion and lifestyle stores worldwide, and its holdings include iShop, reportedly Asia's biggest Apple distributor.
deep_cut_fact: She released a cookbook, 'COMO Simple', in 2025. She was also inducted into the Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (2014) and has chaired Singapore's National Parks Board.

public_contacts.value: louise.james@comohotels.com (Louise James, Global Director of PR, COMO Hotels and Resorts)

notes: Described as extremely private. The Forbes profile is a joint one with her husband Ong Beng Seng, who has his own legal matters in Singapore; keep outreach focused on her. COMO PR is the best route. Wellness, hospitality and Mulberry are the natural podcast angles.

name: Diane Briere de l'Isle
current_role: Chair, Moondance Foundation (Welsh grant-making charity, reg. 1139224)
profile: Diane Briere de l'Isle Engelhardt OBE is married to Henry Engelhardt, founder and former CEO of Cardiff-based car insurer Admiral Group; their fortune comes from Admiral shares after its 2004 LSE flotation. The couple set up the Moondance Foundation in 2010, funded by regularly donating Admiral shares. She chairs it, and it has given away well over £76m, mostly to causes in Wales.
interesting_fact: The Moondance Foundation is funded by gifts of the couple's Admiral shares. When the pandemic hit, she launched a Covid-19 Relief Fund, and the foundation later committed a further £10m to Welsh organisations.
deep_cut_fact: She and Henry Engelhardt received the First Minister's Special Award at the Welsh Government's St David Awards 2026.
notes: Wealth is shared with husband Henry Engelhardt; the Rich List entry is joint. I couldn't verify any formal Admiral role for her, so don't describe her as an Admiral co-founder. The foundation's published contact is the best route. Moondance Cancer Initiative is a related Welsh initiative.

name: Curtis LeRoy Carlson
profile: Curt Carlson (b. 1914) founded Carlson Companies (Gold Bond trading stamps, later Radisson hotels, TGI Friday's and Carlson Wagonlit travel) in Minneapolis. He died on 19 February 1999 at age 84.
notes: DECEASED on 19 Feb 1999 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curt_Carlson; NYT obituary 22 Feb 1999). His daughter Marilyn Carlson Nelson became chair in June 1999, and Carlson is now a family office owned by his daughters. Remaining fields skipped per instructions.

name: Ji Xuewen
current_role: Co-founder and major individual shareholder (7.53% as of Q1 2026) of Shenzhen Dynanonic (SZSE: 300769), a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material maker; no current executive role confirmed
profile: Ji Xuewen co-founded Dynanonic (德方纳米) in 2007 with a RMB500,000 capital contribution alongside two partners. The company became a major supplier of nano-scale LFP cathode material for EV and energy-storage batteries. He was its signing company head around 2020, holding about 20%; his stake has since fallen through transfers to 7.53% (Q1 2026), and Kong Lingyong now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: Dynanonic started in 2007 as a RMB500,000 limited company set up by Ji Xuewen, Yang Haiyan and Wang Yunshi, and grew into a leading supplier of LFP cathode material for China's EV and grid-storage boom.
notes: Very low public profile and no English-language bio found. His stake has fallen sharply (about 20% in 2020 to 7.53% in 2026), so he is likely no longer a billionaire; the Hurun listing was 2022-23 only. 'Alive' is marked unknown only because no personal coverage exists; he is still listed as a shareholder in 2026. Relevant to the energy-storage theme. The only route is company IR.

name: Caspar MacDonald-Hall
current_role: Property investor; director of Proudreed Ltd and London & Cambridge Properties (LCP) group entities
profile: MacDonald-Hall is a Hampshire-based property investor long tied to Kingswinford-based London & Cambridge Properties (LCP), a big Midlands retail and industrial landlord, of which he owned about 40% per a 2013 profile. He also owns 46% of Havant-based holding company Ringmerit and co-owns Southampton investor Proudreed. LCP now trades as part of the M Core platform.
interesting_fact: LCP's holdings include town-centre retail in Dudley and Walsall and industrial estates such as Pensnett, Burntwood and Bloxwich in the Black Country. He also held a reported £31m stake in AIM Aviation.
deep_cut_fact: A keen angler and game shooter, he is described as 'consistently rated as one of the best shots in the country'.

public_contacts.value: https://www.lcpproperties.co.uk (LCP, part of M Core; company site, not personal)

notes: Extremely private, with no interviews or personal web presence found, and his name is spelled several ways (Casper/Caspar, with or without the hyphen). His current link to LCP/M Core after it became part of M Core is unclear. 'Alive' is marked unknown because there is no recent coverage. One search result carried an embedded prompt-injection string, which I ignored.

name: Wang Mingwang
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder, Sunwoda Electronic (SZSE: 300207); brother Wang Wei was re-elected chairman in Sept 2026
profile: Wang Mingwang co-founded Sunwoda in Shenzhen in 1997 with his brother Wang Wei. It grew from phone battery packs into one of China's major lithium-ion battery makers, supplying consumer-electronics battery modules to Apple and Huawei and expanding into EV and energy-storage cells. He is still the controlling shareholder, and the company has filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing (filed July 2025, refiled Jan 2026).
interesting_fact: He is widely called the 'richest man in Maoming', his home city in Guangdong. Sunwoda began making batteries for China's first-generation 'big brick' (大哥大) mobile phones.
deep_cut_fact: Sunwoda's big break came in 1999. After hearing Konka planned own-brand phones, the brothers pitched to make the batteries and finished the sample after '21 sleepless days'. It reportedly beat the benchmark by 40% on quality and was 30% cheaper.
notes: Strong fit for the energy/storage theme. Low media profile with no personal social accounts; go through Sunwoda IR. Avoid the 2026 negative press (profit drop and a large customer battery-quality claim) as a topic.

name: Tan Yu Yeh
current_role: Founder and adviser, Mr D.I.Y. Group (Bursa Malaysia: MRDIY); stepped down as executive vice-chairman in April 2025
profile: Tan Yu Yeh, a University of Malaya physics graduate and former engineer and remisier, opened the first Mr D.I.Y. hardware store in Kuala Lumpur in 2005 with his brother Tan Yu Wei. It became a home-improvement chain of more than 4,000 stores across Asia and Europe, listed in 2020, and its Indonesian unit listed in December 2024. He became an adviser to the group in April 2025 and remains the controlling shareholder through Bee Family Ltd.
interesting_fact: He had no retail experience when he opened the first Mr D.I.Y. on Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, KL, in July 2005. Two more outlets opened within the same year.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, he graduated in physics from the University of Malaya (1996) and worked in engineering at hard-disk media maker Komag USA.
notes: Low-profile founder with no personal social accounts found. Best route is Mr D.I.Y. corporate/IR. Tatler notes his first career in engineering and as a remisier.

name: Joachim Ante
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, Unity Technologies; co-founder and backer of Underground Ventures (Copenhagen geothermal VC)
profile: German-born Joachim 'Joe' Ante co-founded Unity (originally Over the Edge Entertainment) in Copenhagen in 2004 with David Helgason and Nicholas Francis. He wrote much of the engine's core, and Unity became the engine behind games like Pokemon Go and Among Us; it listed on the NYSE in 2020. He is now a climate philanthropist and in 2024 co-founded Underground Ventures, a geothermal-only venture firm.
interesting_fact: Unity began as a failed game project: Ante and his cofounders realised the engine they had built was more valuable to other developers than their game. He began writing the engine's core as a teenager.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Underground Ventures with Torsten Kolind (ex-YouNoodle), and his own money funds it: a $40m vehicle backing early-stage geothermal tech such as drilling, well casings, sensors and underground storage. Portfolio includes Hephae Energy and GA Drilling.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast because of the geothermal angle. Underground Ventures is the most natural route; Torsten Kolind runs investment and has appeared on energy podcasts (Low Carbon Solutions ep. 183). He is also a Founders Pledge member. I found no verified personal social accounts.

name: John Whittaker
current_role: Founder and controlling owner of The Peel Group (UK property, ports, energy and infrastructure). Wikipedia lists him as chairman; Place North West reports Mark Whitworth as group chair since 2023
profile: Born in Bury, Lancashire in 1942, Whittaker built Peel from buying old cotton mills for their land in the 1970s into a conglomerate spanning property, Peel Ports, media and energy. After a long 1980s battle he took control of the Manchester Ship Canal, which led to the Trafford Centre, later sold to Intu in 2011, and MediaCityUK. He lives on the Isle of Man.
interesting_fact: He reportedly persuaded the BBC to move to MediaCityUK at Salford Quays, beating rival Manchester sites.
deep_cut_fact: He was educated at Prior Park College, a Catholic boarding school in Bath, and considered becoming a priest before joining the family building business.

public_contacts.value: egreen@peel.co.uk / kholland@peel.co.uk (Peel Waters media enquiries, a Peel Group business)

notes: Publicity-shy and rarely gives interviews; he is in his 80s. Peel's energy arm (Peel NRE) and ports may be relevant to the podcast. Go through Peel corporate. Wikipedia carries a paid-editing warning. Don't confuse him with a different John Peter Whittaker who is a director of Peel entities.

name: Gao Tianguo
profile: Gao Tianguo (高天国, also Ko Tin Kwok) was the actual controller of Shanghai Guozhijie, the controlling shareholder of Shanghai-listed Anxin Trust, and invested in real estate and energy. Anxin Trust announced that he died of illness on 4 April 2022.
notes: DECEASED on 4 April 2022, per Anxin Trust's announcement (source: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2022-04-05/2203430.html). Identity matched via his Forbes profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/gao-tianguo/). Anxin Trust has since been restructured as Jianyuan Trust. Remaining fields skipped per instructions.
